hints: Focus on what sodium carbonate can and cannot deprotonate at room temperature, think acids versus alcohols.
Identify the one $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ group and check whether the $\text{-OH}$ groups on the ring are phenols or aliphatic alcohols.
Remember that ester hydrolysis needs hot aqueous alkali, so decide which functional group is left untouched by cold carbonate and which forms a sodium salt.
walkthrough:
**List the functional groups present**

Look carefully at chlorogenic acid. It has one carboxylic acid $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$, three alcohol $\text{-OH}$ groups on a saturated ring, and one ester $\text{-COO-}$. The R group is told to take no part.

$$\text{groups = carboxylic acid + aliphatic alcohol + ester}$$

**Recall the reactivity of sodium carbonate**

Sodium carbonate solution is a weak base. It is strong enough to neutralise carboxylic acids in good yield at room temperature to give $\text{-CO}_2\text{Na}$ plus $\text{CO}_2$ and water.

$$\text{R-CO}_2\text{H + Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow \text{R-CO}_2\text{Na + CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Rule out alcohols and esters under these conditions**

Aliphatic alcohols are far less acidic than phenols and do not react with $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$. Esters are hydrolysed only by heating with $\text{NaOH}$, not by cold carbonate solution, so the ester linkage stays intact.

$$\text{R-OH + Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow \text{no reaction (alcohol, not phenol)}$$

**Deduce the product**

Only the carboxylic acid is converted to its sodium salt. All three ring $\text{-OH}$ groups and the ester remain unchanged, which matches the structure with $\text{CO}_2\text{Na}$ alone.

options.A: Correct. Only the carboxylic acid reacts with excess sodium carbonate to give $\text{-CO}_2\text{Na}$. The three groups on the cyclohexane ring are aliphatic alcohols, not phenols, so they do not react, and the ester is not hydrolysed at room temperature.
options.B: Incorrect. This shows every $\text{-OH}$ converted to $\text{-ONa}$ as well as $\text{-CO}_2\text{Na}$. Students choose this by treating aliphatic alcohols like phenols. Sodium carbonate deprotonates phenols and carboxylic acids, but not ordinary alcohols.
options.C: Incorrect. This leaves the carboxylic acid unchanged as $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ while converting all alcohols to $\text{-ONa}$. This is backwards. The carboxylic acid is the most acidic group and is the one that must react in good yield.
options.D: Incorrect. This shows alkaline hydrolysis of the ester into a triol plus an unsaturated acid. Ester hydrolysis requires heating with $\text{NaOH}$, not room temperature sodium carbonate, so no cleavage occurs here.
